The BSW program will take most students 4 years to complete and will include 120 undergraduate credits. The program focuses on preparing entry-level generalist social workers. In alignment with CSWE accreditation standards and institutional academic policies, the BSW Program does not award academic credit for prior life experience or previous professional employment. This policy ensures that all course credit reflects structured academic learning and competency-based evaluation. 

CSWE Accreditation: The curriculum is in the process of pursuing status for CSWE accreditation, with curricula designed to align with the Educational Accreditation Policy Standards and Social Work Competencies. The specific competencies have been highlighted in the curriculum in each course syllabus.

Prerequisites: Students are formally admitted into the program beginning in their 3rd year. Students must complete approximately 60 credits of coursework covering the lower division UCORE requirements. The social work advisor and BSW Program Director will individually assess whether course work taken meets the requirements. SOCL WRK 201 & 202 are encouraged to be taken during the first two years of study; however, they are not required for acceptance into the BSW Program and can be taken during the junior year. SOCL WRK 101, Social Work as a Profession, is a one-credit survey course and is the only optional course in the social work program. Social Work 101 is therefore not required as a prerequisite nor a program requirement.

The social work advisor and BSW Program Director will individually assess whether a transfer student meets the course requirements to fulfill the Direct Transfer Associates (DTA) degree criteria before formal admission to the social work program.

Supporting Courses: Supporting courses for the social work major are required and can be taken during the first two years of study or after being admitted to the social work program. These courses include: Introduction to Sociology/Social Problems (only course work specifically designated as a Sociology course covering Introduction to Sociology or Social Problems will be accepted); Introduction to Psychology; Introduction to Statistics (including differential and inferential statistics); Human Biology; Technical Writing; and two semesters of a foreign language course (two years of high school foreign language satisfies this requirement).

A minimum cumulative 2.5 GPA is required in SOCL WRK courses.
